Genesis (pre-emission) total supply, pinned normatively by R9.7 (§9.3). Components (D-0440, tokenomics workbook rev 2026-08-27; ECON-010 sec. 2.1): miner airdrop 1,200,000,000 + validator airdrop 1,200,000,000 + agent airdrop 1,200,000,000 + ecosystem reserve 800,000,000 = exactly 4,400,000,000. Each component is pinned by its own enforced param below, so the four cannot drift apart from this total. There are no genesis auctions, and Team is NOT genesis-allocated — Labs and Foundation receive a per-block subsidy instead (D-0421). D-0440 resized the pool 3,500,000,000 → 4,400,000,000 to absorb the validator bond raise (validator_min_stake 305,505 → 1,200,000): the bond IS the validator cohort, so at the old pool the four components summed to 3,600,000,000 and the residual reserve went NEGATIVE. Allocation history is in whitepaper/decisions/v0.4.md (D-0421, D-0435, D-0438, D-0440). |\n| `genesis_miner_airdrop` | 1_200_000_000 | FLOP | D-0438 | Miner-airdrop component of the genesis supply (27.27%). One of the three D-0421 airdrops, as re-balanced by D-0435 and re-scaled by D-0438 (ECON-009 sec. 2.1). D-0440 held the absolute grant at 1,200,000,000 while resizing the pool, so only its share moved 34.29% → 27.27% (ECON-010 sec. 2.1). Home: §9.3. The workbook presents it as testnet block reward 559,872,000 + capped testnet fee pool 640,128,000; the fee cap is back-solved so the pool lands on exactly 1,200,000,000, so treat the round pool as the ratified quantity, not as an output of the testnet model. This is the actual testnet→mainnet conversion pool (assignPool in testnet-conversion.ts), so it must not silently diverge from the split; the total (genesis_supply) is enforced above, this pins the component too. |\n| `genesis_validator_airdrop` | 1_200_000_000 | FLOP | D-0440 | Validator-airdrop component of the genesis supply (27.27%). Home: §9.3. D-0435 (tokenomics workbook rev 2026-08-20; ECON-008 sec. 2.3) cut the validator grant to the bond and nothing else: the aggregate bond, granted free and bonded at launch, with no airdrop beyond it. That identity is unchanged — the grant IS validator_min_stake × validator_active_set_cap — so D-0440's bond raise 305,505 → 1,200,000 carries the cohort 305,505,000 → 1,200,000,000 (tokenomics workbook rev 2026-08-27; ECON-010 sec. 2.1). This is what forced the pool resize: at the old 3,500,000,000 the four components summed to 3,600,000,000 and genesis_reserve, the residual leg, went to MINUS 100,000,000. Consumed directly as a conversion pool by assignPool in testnet-conversion.ts (per-cohort pools, not one miner pool), so it is pinned here too: otherwise the validator pool could drift from the ratified split while check_params.py still passed. This CLOSES ECON-009 gap G2 (issue #1353): the bonded stake is the only slashing collateral in the system, and it now grows with the float instead of falling behind it — 12.30% → 8.73% under D-0438, back to 27.27% here. |\n| `genesis_agent_airdrop` | 1_200_000_000 | FLOP | D-0438 | Agent-airdrop component of the genesis supply (27.27%). Home: §9.3. D-0440 held the absolute grant at 1,200,000,000 while resizing the pool, so only its share moved 34.29% → 27.27% (ECON-010 sec. 2.1); gap G1 below is unaffected, the pool size being unchanged. D-0438 (tokenomics workbook rev 2026-08-22; ECON-009 sec. 2.1) doubled it from the 596,030,400 that ECON-007 sec. 3.5 adopted, to a round 1,200,000,000, historically sized as an agent spend cap of 600,000,000 plus a testnet prize pool of 600,000,000 (D-0438 sizing rationale, not the current grant split). Consumed directly as a conversion pool by assignPool in testnet-conversion.ts, so it is pinned here alongside the miner and validator components. Its grants unlock by spend-to-unlock (yellowpaper §8.2 R8.7, D-0522): one FLOP per three FLOP of locked principal spent in settled sessions, spend capped at three quarters of principal, no end block. All Era-0 allocations land as grants (R8.6); across this pool D-0522 caps locked spend at 900,000,000 and unlocked principal at 300,000,000. With no end block, ECON-009 gap G1's demand shortfall slows the unlock rather than breaking a schedule; no code reads spend_to_unlock.agent_ratio_n today (#1354). |\n| `genesis_reserve` | 800_000_000 | FLOP | D-0440 | Ecosystem/incentives reserve component of the genesis supply (18.18%) — KOL, referral and growth incentives. Home: §9.3. NOT an airdrop, so D-0421's \"three airdrops only\" stays intact. Promoted to an enforced param by D-0435 (tokenomics workbook rev 2026-08-20; ECON-008 sec. 2.3): it previously existed only in the simulator, so nothing stopped the four genesis components from drifting away from genesis_supply. It is the residual leg — D-0438 fixed the miner, validator and agent cohorts and this absorbs the rest of the pool, as it absorbed what the D-0435 validator-grant cut freed. D-0440 fixed all three cohorts at 1,200,000,000 and sized the pool so this residual lands on a round 800,000,000 (was 794,495,000; ECON-010 sec. 2.1) — at the pre-resize 3,500,000,000 pool the same residual would have been MINUS 100,000,000. Release cadence per the workbook's Airdrop Schedule sec. 3 is 20% at Season 0 (160,000,000) then eight half-year seasons of 80,000,000 to +48mo; D-0438's four annual tranches of 158,899,000 are superseded. Controller and release rules are still undefined (ECON-008 sec. 7 C7, ECON-009 gap G3) and it has no runtime presence yet. Under D-0531 (closing #1358), the workbook's legacy on-chain referral commission model (6–10%) is superseded by a public explorer leaderboard and periodic referral lotteries funded from this reserve and settled off-chain. |\n| `validator_min_stake` | 1_200_000 | FLOP | D-0440 | Baseline floor (MinimumValidatorStake); flat under D-0539, which removes the former 9%/yr growth (runtime removal #3655). COUPLED to V_booked (realized effective value), NOT to reward — D-0413 (C5). Effective floor enforced at registration + committee admission = max(baseline, k·V_booked), ratcheted (never below baseline, composes with C6 thermostat). baseline = the CoCVoC required-stake requirement: ~1,163,309 FLOP at 96 FLOP/block (Lean Security.lean::CoCVoC.stake_at_current_params; the legacy 305,505 FAILS the deterrence margin — legacy_stake_insufficient_at_r96). THRESHOLD-ROBUST: in the reward-capture requiredStake the corruption fraction θ CANCELS, so 1/3 (the AlephBFT safety threshold, Consensus.quorum_inter_gt_third) vs the earlier '51%' framing barely moves the ~1.16M (51% is a Nakamoto number, not a BFT one). CAVEAT: this reward-pegged base FALLS with each halving (reward_floor_shrinks_across_halving) — it prices reward-capture, not value-at-risk; the DURABLE floor is the value-coupled k·V_booked below, not this baseline. RATIFIED AT 1,200,000 BY D-0440 (tokenomics workbook rev 2026-08-27; ECON-010): the superseded 305,505 predated both the 96-FLOP decision and the V_booked retarget, and Lean already proved it inadequate — legacy_stake_insufficient_at_r96 machine-checks that it FAILS the 1.22x margin at R=96, while scaled_stake_sufficient_at_r96 proves 1,200,000 HOLDS it. The shipped floor is now the value the spec proves sufficient, closing ECON-009 C1 / issue #1353. Because the aggregate bond IS the validator genesis cohort (genesis_validator_airdrop), this raise carried that cohort 305,505,000 -> 1,200,000,000 and forced the genesis_supply resize to 4,400,000,000. Runtime wiring LANDED (pallet_validators::ValueCoupledStakeFloor / effective_minimum_stake / set_value_coupled_floor, #86); k + retarget cadence calibration is governance/ENG-31.
